title: 1. Refinement types
summary: Pre- and postconditions as types, proved at compile time.

lesson.title: A function with a contract
lesson.body: The result of clamp stays between lo and hi. Its second argument requires hi to be at least lo, and the caller must establish that precondition. Vox proves the result contract for every permitted input.
lesson.challenge: Change clamp 0 10 x in bounded to clamp 10 0 x. Check the program, inspect the failed goal, then restore the valid call.
lesson.detail: A result contract describes normal returns. The total mode additionally requires termination and rules out exceptions.

title: 2. Choosing the specification
summary: A true contract can still describe the wrong result.

lesson.title: A proof needs the right question
lesson.body: The width of a window should be stop - start. This implementation returns the whole buffer length. Its weak contract promises only a bounded result, so Vox accepts it. For length = 10, start = 4 and stop = 10, the required width is 6.
lesson.challenge: Add w = stop - start to the result contract. Check the program to see the failure. Then replace the function body with stop - start and check again.
lesson.detail: Verification proves the stated property. Examples and tests help determine whether that property captures the intended behavior.

title: 3. Termination measures
summary: [@@decreases] for Euclid and binary search; Collatz is rejected.

lesson.title: Show that recursion makes progress
lesson.body: A total recursive function needs a decreasing measure. In gcd, the remainder is smaller than b. The final Collatz example is deliberately rejected: n can increase, so n is not a valid measure.
lesson.challenge: Remove collatz_steps to check the two valid functions. Then replace a mod b in gcd with b and inspect why its measure no longer decreases.
lesson.detail: Rejecting a proposed measure does not prove that the function diverges. It means this termination argument did not establish the claim.

title: 4. Lemmas and induction
summary: Definition equations and a proof by induction, erased at call sites.

lesson.title: Prove a fact about every list
lesson.body: The length_append lemma says that concatenation adds lengths. Its recursive call supplies the induction hypothesis. [@def] generates definition equations that the proof explicitly uses.
lesson.challenge: Change x :: append rest ys to append rest ys in append. Check which step of length_append fails, then restore the element.
lesson.detail: A lemma is a function whose result type states a theorem. The client calls it inside ghost_, so the evidence is checked and erased.

title: 5. Ghost code and data
summary: Ghost fields and proof calls disappear from the compiled program.

lesson.title: Keep evidence without storing it
lesson.body: A summary contains a runtime total and a ghost list of its items. The result contracts relate the total to that list. The ghost field supports reasoning without occupying a runtime slot.
lesson.challenge: Open Erased program and find the remaining record fields. Then add let count s = List.length s.items and inspect the rejection of a ghost value used by runtime code.
lesson.detail: Ghost data may affect proofs and contracts. It cannot supply a value needed by executable code.

title: 6. Machine integers
summary: x + 1 > x fails at max_int: ints are 63-bit machine integers.

lesson.title: An arithmetic claim needs a bound
lesson.body: Incrementing max_int wraps to min_int. The precondition on next excludes that case. The otherwise identical succ function has no such precondition and is rejected.
lesson.challenge: Inspect the countermodel under Proof goals. Give succ the same precondition as next, then check again.
lesson.detail: Countermodels assign values to the compiler's logical variables; they are not replayed program executions. This browser build also reports a limitation for integer literals its 32-bit JavaScript host cannot read faithfully.

title: Division by zero
summary: A standard-library precondition that the caller cannot establish.

title: An affine ghost token
summary: A unique ghost permit cannot be used twice.
